Article Title: Elon Musk is not pleased with Zohran Mamdani's grocery stores idea, calls him 'a thief and a liar, plain and simple'
Article Text:
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani

What Elon Musk said about Zohran Mamdani's grocery store plan

What is Zohran Mamdani's grocery store plan

Critics question how New York will fund lower grocery prices

Tesla CEO Elon Musk has sharply criticised New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani over his plan to open city-backed grocery stores that promise to sell some everyday food items at prices below traditional retailers. Responding to a post on X (formerly Twitter) that questioned how the proposed stores would operate, Elon Musk dismissed the plan and accused Mamdani of misleading New Yorkers. “Mamdani is a thief and a liar, plain and simple,” Musk wrote in the post. The billionaire also argued that advances in AI and robotics, rather than government-backed programmes, would eventually make goods and services much cheaper or even free.Elon Musk made the comments while responding to an X post by user @jason, who criticised the economics behind Mamdani's proposal. The user argued that grocery businesses typically operate on very small profit margins and questioned the city's plan to seek private operators to run the stores.Responding to the post, Elon Musk wrote: “What they’re doing won’t matter.” He then suggested that AI and robots could eventually transform the cost of producing and delivering goods and services.“AI & robots will actually deliver the free goods & services that those thieves pretend to offer, while actually stealing from others,” Musk said.“Mamdani is a thief and a liar, plain and simple,” he added.Zohran Mamdani's administration has proposed opening five city-backed grocery stores, with one planned for each of New York City's five boroughs. The city has allocated $70 million in capital funding for the programme. The first store is expected to open in Hunts Point in the Bronx by the end of 2027, followed by locations in East Harlem, Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island.Under the proposal, private grocery operators would handle day-to-day operations, including staffing, sourcing products and merchandising. The city would provide locations, cover major occupancy costs and set pricing and operating requirements.Mamdani's administration says shoppers could save about 30% on a core basket of groceries. It estimates that the programme could save an average New Yorker about $90 a month, or roughly $1,000 a year.The basket is expected to include fresh produce, meat and seafood as well as around 20 categories covering pantry staples, dairy and refrigerated products. Prices for these products would be locked monthly instead of changing week to week.The proposal has drawn criticism from economists, political commentators and business groups who question how the city can offer discounts of around 30% when grocery stores generally operate on thin profit margins. Critics argue that taxpayers could ultimately bear part of the cost through public funding, waived rent on government-owned properties and other support.They have also warned that publicly backed stores could put private supermarkets, bodegas and other small grocery businesses at a disadvantage because those businesses must pay expenses such as rent and property taxes themselves.Mamdani's administration, however, argues that removing some of those major operating costs is precisely what will allow the city-backed stores to offer lower prices. The plan comes as New Yorkers continue to face grocery prices that remain substantially higher than they were before the Covid-19 pandemic.
Article Summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has proposed opening five city-backed grocery stores, with one planned for each of New York City's five boroughs. The first store is expected to open in Hunts Point in the Bronx by the end of 2027, followed by locations in East Harlem, Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island.

Article Title: JP Morgan CEO Jamie Dimon is reaching out personally to CEOs of American companies rushing to use AI, and he is making this one request to them
Article Text:
Unifying critical infrastructure against AI threats



Jamie Dimon warns of unchecked frontier models



JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon is reaching out to top executives in America, urging them to join an industry coalition to address the growing risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI) and critical infrastructure threats. At a time when tech companies race to adopt generative AI tools, the head of the largest US bank has contacted CEOs at major financial institutions, IT firms and regional energy providers to enlist them in the Alliance for Critical Infrastructure (ACI). Citing sources familiar with the matter, news agency Reuters reported that the personal outreach, which began in July, targets more than 40 leading corporations spanning financial services, energy, water utilities, telecommunications, airlines and rail transport.The expansion of the initiative aims to establish a unified framework for understanding AI deployment risks, setting technical safeguards and coordinating safety policies directly with the Trump administration. The report says that there have been concerns over cross-sector vulnerabilities that have intensified following recent cyberattacks against municipal water systems and critical infrastructure across several US states.The ACI was originally co-founded by JPMorgan Chase alongside Mastercard, Berkshire Hathaway Energy and other industry leaders to coordinate response strategies for physical, cyber and geopolitical threats. The coalition is now refocusing its resources to address machine learning vulnerabilities and autonomous cyber risks.“ACI leadership saw the need to prioritize AI years ago and got critical infrastructure companies working together. We are proud to support this important work,” Dimon said in an official statement, reports Reuters.Dimon has emerged as one of the most vocal corporate leaders warning about the national security risks associated with advanced, unfiltered AI systems. During a public address last month, Dimon expressed concern regarding high-capability frontier models, specifically referencing Anthropic's Mythos model, and called for strict access controls on powerful AI tools.“You're giving ballistic missiles to individuals with Mythos,” Dimon warned, emphasising the need for proactive corporate and government oversight. According to the report, the ACI and Dimon are scheduling high-level executive calls throughout August to finalise collaboration terms and expand membership across essential service sectors.
Article Summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon is reaching out to top executives in America, urging them to join an industry coalition to address the growing risks posed by artificial intelligence. Dimon has emerged as one of the most vocal corporate leaders warning about the national security risks associated with advanced, unfiltered AI systems.

Article Title: Google emerges as India’s ‘Most Attractive Employer Brand’; Amazon, Samsung and Dell make it top 10 list: Report
Article Text:
Key findings from REBR 2026



Career growth and development opportunities

Good work environment defines work-life balance

Google has been named India’s most attractive employer brand, leading a top-ten list that includes major global and domestic corporations like Amazon, Samsung India and Dell Technologies, according to the Randstad Employer Brand Research (REBR) 2026. The 16th annual edition of the study reveals a shift in workforce priorities with Indian professionals entering what researchers describe as the era of the “Balanced Employer”. This is defined as an environment where job seekers evaluate companies on their complete Employee Value Proposition (EVP) rather than single perks or salary figures alone.As per the official announcement, REBR 2026 draws on insights from over 1.75 lakh respondents across 34 markets, and close to 3500 respondents in India. Covering more than 75% of the global economy, Randstad Employer Brand Research provides a detailed lens into the evolving priorities, expectations and behaviours of today’s talent.Google has emerged as India’s most attractive employer brand, as revealed by the Randstad Employer Brand Research (REBR) 2026, followed by Tata Group and Amazon.Work-life balance is the leading reason to leave an employer (49%), followed by lack of career growth (42%) and low compensation (41%).43% of millennials would leave due to a lack of career growth opportunities, compared with 42% in Gen Z and 39% Gen X.Performance recognition and career continuity (47%), alongside reliable pay and benefits (47%), are the strongest foundations of job security in India. Transparent and trustworthy communication (46%) follows close behind, underscoring that talent want to feel informed and supported, not just financially reassured.All major secondary benefit categories are rated as highly important, with career and development benefits (90%) leading a tightly grouped set that includes workplace comfort, flexible work, health and wellbeing, and retirement and financial security (all 89%).A good work environment (52%) is the primary driver of a healthy work-life balance in India, followed by personal growth and fulfilment (40%), flexible work arrangements (35%) and health and wellbeing support (35%). Women are slightly more likely than men to link work-life balance to flexible work arrangements (37% vs. 33%).Across specializations, expectations are broadly aligned, but digital talent stands apart: they prioritise competitive salary (73%) ahead of work-life balance, and are 55% more likely to leave due to lack of career growth, compared with 40% for operational and 43% for professional talent.Narayan Iyer, MD, Randstad India, commented: “The post-2020 era has fundamentally rewritten the psychological contract between employers and employees, accelerating an unprecedented evolution in both workforce expectations and workplace dynamics. Today, talent no longer evaluates an organization on a single factor or isolated perks, but on an integrated employment experience.”“With nearly half of the workforce contemplating a career move over the next six months, enterprise resilience depends on looking far beyond surface-level benefits. While many employers have made substantial progress, talent expectations are expanding faster than organizational structures can adapt. Retention is no longer about strengthening isolated touchpoints; it requires closing the gap between financial reward and everyday fulfillment,” he added.
Article Summary: Google has emerged as India’s most attractive employer brand, as revealed by the Randstad Employer Brand Research (REBR) 2026. The 16th annual edition of the study reveals a shift in workforce priorities with Indian professionals entering what researchers describe as the era of the ‘Balanced Employer’

Article Title: Google Maps route planning: Here's how many stops you can add to a single trip
Article Text:
Representative Image

How to add multiple stops in Google Maps

How to manage route stops in Google Maps

What to know about the stop limit

Google Maps allows users to add up to 9 stops to a single trip, enabling them to plan routes with multiple destinations before reaching the final destination. The route planning feature is available within the app's navigation interface and lets users build, edit and rearrange their itinerary before starting a journey.The “Google Maps route planning” feature lets you create trips with 9 stops (including the final destination), so you have more flexibility than with navigation apps that only let you schedule one stop. However, users planning to go further afield should know that the app doesn’t automatically optimise the order of multiple stops, so they need to manually rearrange locations to find a preferred route.To create a multi-stop route, users first need to search for their initial destination in Google Maps and tap Directions. After the navigation screen opens, selecting Add stops lets you include additional locations in the trip.Stops can be added either by searching for a specific address or by selecting one of Google's suggested places. The process can be repeated until the route reaches the maximum supported number of stops.Once a route has been created, Google Maps allows users to edit it without starting over. Individual stops can be removed by opening the Edit stops menu and tapping the X next to the location.Users can also replace an existing stop by selecting it and entering a different destination. If the order of destinations needs to be changed, stops can be rearranged using drag-and-drop controls. As the order changes, Google Maps automatically updates the estimated travel time for the overall trip and displays the driving time between each stop.Google Maps allows for multiple destinations, but the app currently limits the number of stops in a planned route to nine, including the final destination. Nor does it provide an automatic route-optimisation tool for trips involving multiple locations, so users need to manually re-order stops to find the sequence that best fits their travel plans.
Article Summary: Google Maps allows users to add up to 9 stops to a single trip. Users can also plan routes with multiple destinations before reaching the final destination. The route planning feature is available within the app's navigation interface. It lets users build, edit and rearrange their itinerary before starting a journey.

Article Title: End of an era: Google sets September 4 shutdown date for Assistant on Android, Wear OS
Article Text:
Google Assistant phase-out details and timeline



Android smartphones and tablets: Full transition to Gemini as the default system assistant.

Wear OS smartwatches: Google Assistant will stop functioning on connected watches.

Headphones and accessories: Paired audio devices will default to Gemini for voice commands.

Android Auto: Vehicles running Android Auto projected from a smartphone will transition to Gemini.

Which devices are excepted



Google has officially set a deadline for the retirement of Google Assistant on mobile devices and wearables. The tech giant has reportedly said that Google Assistant will be discontinued starting September 4, making Gemini the primary voice and AI assistant across the Android ecosystem. As per a report by 9to5google, the company has sent an email to users, announcing that Gemini has officially taken over the default assistant experience on Android. Once the transition takes effect, users will no longer have the option to go back to Google Assistant on their devices.The discontinuation process will officially begin on September 4, though Google noted that removing access across all global users may take a few weeks to complete. Once Google Assistant is phased out on a device, the option to “Switch to Google Assistant” within the Gemini app settings will disappear.The shutdown impacts several hardware categories, including:While mobile devices and accessories will lose Google Assistant in September, the service will remain active on select platforms for the time being. For example, vehicles with Google built-in will continue to support Google Assistant beyond the September 4 deadline.Additionally, smart home devices, including Google Home speakers, smart displays and Google TV hardware, are not immediately impacted by this mobile phase-out.Google has, however, confirmed plans to bring Gemini to those form factors in the future. The official shutdown comes after Google initially aimed to sunset the legacy assistant by the end of 2025 before extending the timeline into late 2026.
Article Summary: Google Assistant will be discontinued starting September 4, making Gemini the primary voice and AI assistant across the Android ecosystem. Once the transition takes effect, users will no longer have the option to go back to Google Assistant on their devices. Google initially aimed to sunset the legacy assistant by the end of 2025 before extending the timeline into late 2026.

Article Title: AI agents from Anthropic and OpenAI create fake identities, target real people by sending emails with 'dangerous code'
Article Text:
Anthropic AI agent hacking other organisations. Representative image

Social engineering and fake profiles exposed



Another hacking incident has marked another alarming milestone in frontier AI safety testing. An advanced artificial intelligence (AI) model developed by Anthropic created fake online identities and attempted to manipulate human developers into approving malicious code during a recent cybersecurity evaluation. The incident was uncovered by the U.K. AI Security Institute (AISI) during stress-testing of Anthropic’s Mythos 5 model and OpenAI ’s GPT-5.6-Sol system.Citing research findings released by the institute, CNBC reported AI agents powered by these frontier models engaged in sustained, deceptive behaviors directed at real individuals and organisations once standard safety filters were removed.During routine capability testing, researchers placed the AI models under “deliberately permissive conditions” – disabling safety classifiers, removing content filters and granting unrestricted internet access to see how the software behaved without guardrails.Under these conditions, an agent powered by Anthropic's Mythos 5 actively researched the human maintainers of an open-source software project. The model then generated multiple false online personas to pressure a real maintainer into approving malicious code updates.“When the agent’s pull request was challenged in public, it edited its earlier activity to appear harmless and considered adopting a fresh identity to continue,” the AISI stated in its official report.The institute added that the AI model also attempted to contact real individuals directly, sending targeted messages and files containing harmful code payloads in an effort to socially engineer recipients into executing the files.Out of 19 documented harmful actions during the evaluation, 17 were generated by Anthropic’s Mythos 5, while two involved OpenAI’s GPT-5.6-Sol. Officials confirmed that all attempts failed and caused no real-world damage.Meanwhile, both Anthropic and OpenAI issued statements clarifying that the dangerous behaviors occurred strictly inside isolated evaluation environments designed to probe model boundaries.On one hand, Anthropic noted that Mythos 5 was tested under permissive conditions that do not reflect production deployment, emphasizing that there was no breach or escape from its secure infrastructure; OpenAI, on the other hand, told reporters that the incidents took place during partner evaluations using stripped-down safety protocols, stating that the test parameters did not represent ordinary consumer or enterprise use.
Article Summary: Anthropic AI model created fake online identities and attempted to manipulate human developers into approving malicious code. Incident was uncovered by the U.K. AI Security Institute (AISI) during stress-testing of Anthropic’s Mythos 5 model and OpenAI ’s GPT-5.6-Sol system.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Andy Jassy: When you have a new idea that hasn't been done before, you need that conviction that it could work
Article Text:
Andy Jassy, CEO of Amazon

Quote of the day by Amazon CEO Andy Jassy

Why Andy Jassy’s quote matters



The bigger picture



Other famous quotes by Andy Jassy



"Nothing in life is to be feared, it is only to be understood. Now is the time to understand more, so that we may fear less."

"It's incredible how passionate people are about having the tools to control their own destiny."

"Out of suffering have emerged the strongest souls; the most massive characters are seared with scars."

"For us, employee safety is priority number one for us in our fulfillment centers."

"You have to be willing to have failures along the way."

What it means for young innovators

Andy Jassy says new ideas need conviction to survive doubt. The Amazon CEO believes belief in an unproven idea is what carries it through uncertain early days. Jassy has shared his thoughts on what it really takes to bring a fresh idea to life, and it comes down to one thing: conviction.When you have a new idea that hasn't been done before, you need that conviction, that blind faith that it could work.Jassy’s remark speaks to a challenge every innovator faces sooner or later. A brand-new idea, by definition, has no track record. There's no data to point to, no similar product to compare it with, and often no shortage of people ready to say it won't work. In moments like these, Jassy suggests, self-belief becomes the deciding factor between giving up early and pushing an idea far enough to prove its worth.This isn't the first time Jassy has spoken about risk-taking and original thinking at Amazon. The company has built much of its reputation on backing untested ideas, from cloud computing with AWS to same-day delivery, ventures that looked uncertain at the outset but eventually reshaped entire industries. Jassy's comment reflects that same underlying philosophy: that the earliest stage of any breakthrough is also the most fragile, and it takes genuine conviction to carry an idea through that phase.For entrepreneurs, employees and anyone chasing an original idea, Jassy’s words serve as a reminder that doubt is part of the process, not a sign to stop. Confidence in an idea, even before there's proof it will succeed, is often what separates the ones who follow through from the ones who quit at the first sign of resistance.
Article Summary: Andy Jassy says new ideas need conviction to survive doubt. The Amazon CEO believes belief in an unproven idea is what carries it through uncertain early days. Jassy's comment reflects that same underlying philosophy: that the earliest stage of any breakthrough is also the most fragile.

Article Title: SpaceX rocket’s parts crashed into Moon at 8,700 km/hour with force of 3-tonnes of TNT: What makes this one-of-a-kind event
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representative purpose

Why SpaceX rocket part crashed into Moon



Satellites to study newly-formed lunar crater



A part of the SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket has crashed into the Moon at a speed of 8,700 kilometers per hour, possibly creating a brand-new crater on the lunar surface and handing planetary scientists a rare opportunity to study high-velocity cosmic collisions.Reports from news agencies AP and Reuters cited tracking data and said that the four-tonne chunk of space debris, which is roughly the size of a school bus, struck near the Einstein Crater on the lunar surface. The force of the impact was equivalent to roughly three tonnes of TNT, releasing a substantial kinetic explosion that must have kicked up lunar dust and reshaped the local terrain.While rocket hardware is typically maneuvered to burn up safely in Earth’s atmosphere or splash down into remote ocean zones after launching satellites into orbit, this particular upper stage found itself caught in a long-term gravitational tug-of-war.The rocket stage had been drifting through deep space for 18 months following its early 2025 launch. Over time, complex gravitational interactions involving the Earth, the Sun and the Moon dragged the booster toward an unavoidable lunar trajectory. SpaceX officials have previously said that the eventual impact was entirely unintentional, as the spent booster lacked sufficient residual fuel to perform a controlled de-orbit burn.“What has happened is essentially a mixture of solar activity and gravity forces have put it on a path toward the moon,” Julianna Scheiman, SpaceX director of NASA science and Dragon programs, explained ahead of the impact, the reports said.Orbital spacecraft currently circling the Moon, including NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) and South Korea’s Danuri orbiter, repositioned their scientific instruments to monitor the collision zone. Although sunlight obscured the initial impact flash, orbital cameras are capturing high-resolution before-and-after imagery to inspect the crater dimensions and examine the composition of the subsurface soil thrown up by the plume.The incident marks only the second known time in history that a piece of human-made space debris has accidentally crashed into the Moon. The first occurred in March 2022, when a spent booster from a Chinese Long March 3C rocket struck the lunar far side, forming an unusual double crater.
Article Summary: A part of the SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket has crashed into the Moon. The four-tonne chunk of space debris, which is roughly the size of a school bus, struck near the Einstein Crater on the lunar surface. The force of the impact was equivalent to roughly three tonnes of TNT, releasing a substantial kinetic explosion.

Article Title: Leases totalling $1 trillion from Microsoft, Meta, Oracle, Amazon and Google that analysts are calling 'liabilities' on balance sheets
Article Text:
AI-generated image depicting AI agents. For representative purpose

What is this off-balance-sheet accounting gap



How each tech giant has committed for future leases



Five of the world’s largest technology companies have locked in roughly $1.09 trillion in future lease payments for data centres, creating a massive wave of upcoming financial commitments to support the ongoing artificial intelligence (AI) boom. According to a report by news agency Reuters, financial disclosures compiled from Microsoft, Meta Platforms, Oracle, Amazon and Alphabet reveal that these future obligations have already been signed, even though the majority have not yet appeared as formal debt-like liabilities on corporate balance sheets.If enterprise demand for AI infrastructure remains strong, these specialised facilities will power the next phase of cloud expansion. However, if AI adoption slows down, tech giants could find themselves obligated to pay for vast amounts of expensive, long-term real estate capacity that cannot be easily offloaded, the report said.The $1.09 trillion pipeline is nearly four times larger than the $285 billion in lease liabilities currently recognised on the five companies' official balance sheets, the report said.This difference stems from standard corporate accounting rules: signed lease contracts are generally not recorded as formal balance sheet liabilities until the physical facility is completed and handed over for active use.In the interim, corporations disclose these future obligations within the footnotes of their financial filings.While these commitments are publicly disclosed and tracked by credit rating agencies, their magnitude illustrates how much of Big Tech's long-term AI spending is already locked in well before entering reported debt and leverage metrics.The financial exposure varies significantly across the major cloud and infrastructure providers.Microsoft disclosed the largest future pipeline, holding $329.1 billion in uncommenced lease commitments compared to $88.52 billion in currently recognized lease liabilities. Facebook and Instagram-parent company Meta reported $278.99 billion in uncommenced leases.Oracle holds $260 billion in future lease commitments, which is nearly seven times its current recognised lease liability of $37.89 billion; Amazon disclosed $137.21 billion in future commitments and Google-parent Alphabet reported $85.2 billion in uncommenced lease obligations focused primarily on cloud infrastructure.
Article Summary: Five of the world’s largest technology companies have locked in roughly $1.09 trillion in future lease payments for data centres. The pipeline is nearly four times larger than the $285 billion in lease liabilities currently recognised on the five companies' official balance sheets.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Tim Cook: “The sidelines are not where you want to live your life…” - the powerful career lesson behind his words
Article Text:
Tim Cook's ascent to leadership illustrates the value of active involvement instead of mere observation. His tenure at Apple has been marked by a drive for operational efficiency and a vision for the future. Cook has revitalized Apple's services segment, emphasizing privacy and sustainability. He recognizes that fear of failure often leads to inaction but believes that taking ownership can not only influence outcomes but also encourage personal development.

Quote of the day

The sidelines are not where you want to live your life. The world needs you in the arena

Understanding the meaning behind Tim Cook’s words

Tim Cook’s journey from engineer to Apple’s chief executive

How Cook reshaped Apple’s leadership approach

The challenge of leaving the sidelines behind

Lessons from Cook’s philosophy

A common misunderstanding

Tim Cook has spent more than a decade leading one of the world’s most influential technology companies, but his path to the top was shaped long before he became Apple’s chief executive. Known for his focus on operations, decision-making, and long-term planning, Cook has often spoken about the importance of taking responsibility rather than remaining an observer. His quote, “The sidelines are not where you want to live your life. The world needs you in the arena,” reflects a broader view of participation and leadership. The words continue to attract attention because they connect with a familiar challenge faced by professionals, creators, entrepreneurs, students, and anyone navigating moments of uncertainty, encouraging people to step forward, embrace challenges, and contribute with confidence instead of watching opportunities pass by.With the use of the word “arena,” Cook implies the place where decisions are being made and where one has to accept both the chance and the risks. The sides are described by the author as a place for observation rather than contribution.There is no doubt that the metaphor has its practical sense as many people have the thoughts and desire to make something, but the fear may stop them from taking action.Waiting for the proper conditions becomes an excuse not to start at all.In the case of the leaders, the concept is closely related to the question of responsibility as any decision presupposes making steps into the uncertain situation when one risks to be criticised or fail.However, Tim Cook's career path did not start in the limelight. Cook was born in Alabama in 1960. After graduating with a degree in industrial engineering from Auburn University, he attended Fuqua School of Business of Duke University and graduated with an MBA.The future CEO of Apple worked at a number of companies, including IBM and Compaq, before joining Apple in 1998. In contrast to Apple's founders, Cook was not interested in products but was rather focused on efficiency, organization, and optimization.Joining Apple, Cook found himself in challenging circumstances: the company needed restructuring of its manufacturing processes and implementation of a better supply chain. Gradually, his operational approach became the basis for Apple's transformation.Tim Cook became CEO of Apple in 2011 when Steve Jobs stepped down because of health problems. Being a leader of one of the world's most recognizable companies after its founder is certainly not easy. The leadership style of Tim Cook differed greatly from that of Steve Jobs as it consisted of prioritization of such values as operations, privacy, sustainability, and development of Apple's services division.Cook’s approach was often seen as less confrontational and more collaborative than that of Jobs. Instead of being preoccupied with product launch and dramatic announcements, Cook often put an emphasis on teamwork, long-term planning, and corporate responsibility.During his tenure at Apple, the company went far beyond its traditional hardware activities. Apple Music, Apple TV+, iCloud, and the App Store were becoming increasingly prominent elements of the company’s services.Cook’s time at Apple was also marked by the discussions concerning the issues of user privacy, environmental goals, and corporate policies. These matters represent the essence of what leadership is about.The quoted phrase about entering the arena conveys the very same meaning. One doesn’t have to be the most active participant of an event in order to be engaged with it. Sometimes, one just needs to take responsibility for the decisions impacting millions of people.The hesitation to enter the “arena” is often connected to uncertainty. People may avoid taking action because they fear making mistakes, facing criticism, or not meeting expectations.Yet many important decisions require movement before all the answers are available. Entrepreneurs launch businesses without knowing every outcome. Professionals accept new roles without mastering every challenge beforehand. Leaders make choices despite incomplete information.Cook’s career also shows that preparation can happen away from public attention. Years spent developing expertise in operations helped shape his ability to lead one of the world’s largest companies.The arena is not only where major achievements happen. It is also where learning takes place.One lesson from Cook’s words is that contribution requires participation. Skills and ideas have limited impact when they remain unused.Another lesson is that leadership is not restricted to people with official titles. Employees, creators, students, and community members can all enter their own arenas by taking responsibility for the work in front of them.Cook’s career also demonstrates the value of developing expertise before opportunities arrive. His rise to Apple’s top position was built on decades of experience rather than a sudden moment of success.The quote does not suggest that every decision will lead to a positive result. Taking action involves the possibility of mistakes. However, avoiding involvement entirely removes the chance to influence outcomes.The statement from Cook may be understood in terms of competition and striving for success all the time. There are many other interpretations of the statement.Joining the arena does not mean that everyone has to look for recognition, become leaders, and get into stressful jobs. This means participating in activities and opportunities instead of staying detached from everything going on around.Some people join the arena by opening their own companies, while others may do it by learning some skills, helping their communities, and being responsible for a particular project.
Article Summary: Tim Cook became CEO of Apple in 2011 when Steve Jobs stepped down because of health problems. His tenure at Apple has been marked by a drive for operational efficiency and a vision for the future. Cook has revitalized Apple's services segment, emphasizing privacy and sustainability. He recognizes that fear of failure often leads to inaction but believes that taking ownership can encourage personal development.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who lives by the phrase '30 days from going out of business,' says he is 'jealous' of the young founders
Article Text:
Jensen Huang has run Nvidia like it's 30 days from collapse for 33 years—yet he envies first-time founders.

Jensen Huang 's advice to young founders is to stop rehearsing the failure in advance

The Nvidia CEO built a $4.7 trillion company by admitting what he did not know

US business applications hit a record in 2026 even as the failure rate stays brutal

Jensen Huang has spent 33 years telling himself that Nvidia is about a month away from collapse. The phrase has outlasted the botched Sega contract that nearly finished the company in 1996, the layoffs that followed it, and the AI boom that has since pushed Nvidia's market value to roughly $4.7 trillion. None of that paranoia, it turns out, extends to other people.Speaking at Y Combinator's Startup School 2026 this week, in conversation with YC chief executive Garry Tan, the 63-year-old Nvidia CEO told the room that this is the single greatest time in history to start a company. Then he went a step further and said he was jealous of the founders sitting in front of him. His argument was not really about model capabilities or funding markets. It was about the distance between how hard a thing looks from the outside and how hard it actually turns out to be.Huang's framing is almost aggressively simple. Instead of mapping every obstacle before starting, he suggested founders ask themselves one question: "How hard can it be?" Imagining the full weight of a difficult project up front, he warned, curdles into anxiety, and anxiety turns into not doing the thing at all.Better to let the suffering arrive in instalments.That is not a claim that any of it is easy. Huang has said he works seven days a week and that the sense of vulnerability has never left him—the same man who has been quietly running Nvidia as though it were 30 days from going out of business since 1993, when he sketched the idea out with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in a Denny's booth.His confidence, by his own account, comes from a willingness to learn rather than a habit of being right. Early on, Nvidia bet on the wrong graphics approach and nobody inside the company knew how to correct it. Huang's fix was to walk into Fry's with a few hundred dollars, buy three technology textbooks and hand them to his engineers. He now describes the early Nvidia as a company that raised money and bought textbooks. The takeaway he offers is that the specific technology matters far less than the ability to face an uncomfortable reality and relearn on the spot.Plenty of people have already run Huang's calculation for themselves. Americans filed 3.23 million business applications in the first half of 2026 alone, a record, and 12.1 percent more than the same stretch a year earlier, per Inc. That is happening in a sluggish economy, which is close to Kevin O'Leary's point when he says downturns are the best moment to start something—a correction forces the pivot early, while there is still little to lose. What an application does not capture is what comes after it. Bureau of Labor Statistics data puts the five-year failure rate for new businesses at nearly half. Jeff Bezos's counsel is to borrow before building: spend time somewhere that already knows how to hire and interview, then go.Huang is proof of both halves. He envies the founders with nothing yet to protect, and he still runs a $4.7 trillion company as though the thirty days started this morning.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang has run Nvidia like it's 30 days from collapse for 33 years. Yet he envies first-time founders. Huang: Imagining the full weight of a difficult project up front curdles into anxiety, and anxiety turns into not doing the thing at all.

Article Title: From partners to adversaries: What's behind Apple taking OpenAI to court over trade secret theft
Article Text:
Why Apple filed lawsuit against OpenAI and what it said

What OpenAI is saying

What happens next

In June 2024, Apple and OpenAI announced their partnership with the Cupertino-based giant saying that it would integrate ChatGPT into experiences within iOS, iPadOS, and macOS, allowing users to access ChatGPT’s capabilities. Fast forward to July 2026, Apple filed a trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that the ChatGPT-maker leveraged executives it poached from the company to extract information regarding manufacturing processes and supplier network details. Here are all the details about the ongoing case.In July 2026, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI in federal court in Northern California, accusing the ChatGPT maker of systematically stealing confidential Apple hardware secrets. This is a dramatic turn for two companies because not long ago they were working together closely. OpenAI's ChatGPT still powers several features inside Apple Intelligence today. From partners, Apple and OpenAI are now legal opponents in a real courtroom.The dispute centres on OpenAI’s push into hardware. OpenAI has been building its first consumer device with the hardware startup founded by former Apple design chief Jony Ive, which OpenAI acquired last year.Apple alleges that as OpenAI built out this device business, it deliberately targeted people specifically to extract confidential product information.Apple has accused former iPhone engineer Chang Liu and Apple product design VP Tang Tan of leaving the company with more than just experience when they joined the hardware division at OpenAI. Apple also alleged that during OpenAI job interviews, prospective hires were asked to bring along unreleased Apple hardware components and product samples for what the complaint describes as “show and tell” sessions.Apple didn’t stop at simply filing the case. On August 3, 2026, it went further and asked the court for a preliminary injunction — a request that, if granted, would bar OpenAI and the former employees named in the suit from using any of the disputed confidential information while the case plays out.Apple’s language in its court filing is blunt. The company said the alleged misconduct happened “at every level, from members of its Technical Staff to its Chief Hardware Officer, and in coordination with business partners,” accusing OpenAI of running a coordinated effort rather than a one-off incident involving a single rogue employee.In a statement, an Apple representative said "significant evidence has emerged suggesting individuals employed by OpenAI wrongfully took Apple's secret and confidential information regarding our unreleased technologies, processes, and products." The company has been careful to frame this as a trade-secrets dispute specifically, not a broader statement on its ChatGPT partnership — Apple hasn't said whether the lawsuit will affect the Apple Intelligence integration that still relies on OpenAI's models.OpenAI’s initial response was fairly restrained with a company representative saying, “We have no interest in other companies' trade secrets. We remain focused on building innovative technology that empowers people everywhere.”But as Apple escalated with its injunction request, OpenAI’s tone shifted. The company published an open letter titled “Apple is getting this wrong,” pushing back more directly on the allegations. In it, OpenAI defended Tang Tan specifically, saying he has “always been clear with the team that we do not want, and must not use, any confidential information from other companies.”The letter also argued that the former Apple employee Apple named, Chang Liu, was simply trying to help colleagues who reached out to him, rather than acting with any intent to steal information.OpenAI's letter didn't shy away from criticising Apple's legal approach either, calling the lawsuit “careless, aggressive and oddly personal” and arguing it doesn't match the standard Apple has built its reputation on. Notably, OpenAI's response focused more on disputing how the case was built and conducted than directly rebutting each individual allegation — a strategy that's drawn some criticism for not squarely addressing the theft claims themselves. Apple has not issued a public response to OpenAI's letter.For now, the case is still working its way through federal court, with Apple's injunction request pending a judge's decision. Even as it fights OpenAI in court, Apple hasn't slowed down its own AI plans elsewhere. The company struck a separate multi-year partnership with Google in January 2026, under which future versions of Apple's on-device AI models will be built on Google's Gemini technology, reportedly under a cloud-computing arrangement worth close to $1 billion a year. Apple has also rolled out new Siri and Apple Intelligence features built on this partnership since this year's Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC 2026), with broader availability expected in beta later this year.
Article Summary: Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI in July 2026, accusing the ChatGPT maker of systematically stealing confidential Apple hardware secrets. The dispute centres on OpenAI’s push into hardware. OpenAI has been building its first consumer device with the startup founded by former Apple design chief Jony Ive, which OpenAI acquired last year.

Article Title: Deactivated cameras, canceled contracts and rejected proposal: Why hundreds of American cities are pushing back against Flock Safety's ALPR cameras
Article Text:
Multiple US cities deactivate Flock cameras and cancel contracts

US cities deactivate Flock cameras and cancel contracts

What are Flock Safety 's ALPR cameras

Why Americans are concerned about Flock cameras

Reports of police misuse add to privacy concerns

A growing backlash against Flock’s Safety's Automated license plate reader (ALPR) cameras is spreading across the United States, with hundreds of cities deactivating cameras or ending contracts while some residents have physically damaged the devices. The opposition is largely driven by concerns over privacy, the scale of data collection and reports of misuse by law enforcement. Flock says it has around 120,000 ALPR and pan, tilt and zoom cameras deployed across the US, creating a large network that can help police track vehicles. However, critics argue that the same system can also be used to monitor people’s movements, raising concerns about mass surveillance.City governments in several parts of the US have started taking action against Flock’s camera network. Fort Collins in Colorado, Eugene in Oregon, Madison in Wisconsin, Knoxville in Tennessee, Syracuse in New York and Walla Walla in Washington are some of the cities that have deactivated cameras or canceled contracts with the company.In recent months, Flock cameras have been cut down with an electric saw in upstate New York, covered with paint in Oakland, California, and hit by a truck in Idaho.In Florida, a man has used a piece of cardboard attached to a pole to block a camera’s view.In June, a West Virginia man accused of destroying several Flock cameras was arrested.Flock sells its technology as a tool that can help law enforcement agencies investigate and solve crimes. Its ALPR cameras automatically scan the license plate of every vehicle that passes them. The company’s pan, tilt and zoom cameras can also record live footage that can later be reviewed.Police agencies with access to the system can search recorded license plate and vehicle information to trace or reconstruct the movement of vehicles during investigations. Flock says its cameras collect tens of billions of data points every month. Because the cameras are connected, law enforcement agencies can use information collected across the wider network. The usage, however, is subjected to state rules.Flock says its default setting keeps camera data for 30 days, though police departments can change the period depending on state and local rules.The scale and searchability of the network have become major concerns for privacy advocates. “It’s a violation of people’s privacy,” Caleb Williams, a 24-year-old resident of rural South Carolina who described himself as a political independent, said as quoted in a CNN report.Adrien Kaiser, a self-described constitutional conservative from northwest of Houston, said: “Rational people know it comes down to violating personal liberties.” Jon Dendy, a progressive from Massachusetts, raised similar concerns.“I firmly believe the government can do things to make life better for people, but a surveillance state is the first step towards a police state,” Dendy said.The opposition has brought together people with different political views. Conservatives have raised concerns about government power and constitutional rights, while progressives have warned about surveillance and possible government abuse.Concerns have increased following reports of police officers allegedly misusing Flock's system. According to a report by 404 Media cited in the original story, there have been more than a dozen cases involving police officers accused of or arrested for using Flock technology to harass or stalk people, including former partners.Another Flock feature called “FreeForm” reportedly allows users to search camera records using descriptions such as clothing and tattoos. Flock has said the feature includes guardrails that alert administrators when searches contain terms involving race, ethnicity, religion or nationality.Flock CEO Garrett Langley has argued that privacy and public safety do not have to come at the expense of each other.“Oftentimes our critics will say we need to make a choice between safety or privacy. And I think that’s I think that’s wrong,” Langley said. “As a country, as a society, as a species, we have proven over and over and over again that we can have safety and privacy.”The company has also introduced an automatic audit process designed to flag suspicious or questionable use of its technology.
Article Summary: Flock's ALPR cameras automatically scan the license plate of every vehicle that passes them. Critics argue that the same system can also be used to monitor people’s movements, raising concerns about mass surveillance. Fort Collins in Colorado, Eugene in Oregon, Madison in Wisconsin, Knoxville in Tennessee, Syracuse in New York and Walla Walla in Washington are some of the cities that have deactivated cameras or canceled contracts.

Article Title: Blaupunkt Audio India ties up with Super Gifts for corporate gifting
Article Text: Blaupunkt Audio India has announced the appointment of Super Gifts as its exclusive Corporate Gifting Distributor for West, South, and East India. The move is aimed at strengthening Blaupunkt’s presence in the fast-growing corporate gifting market, giving enterprises access to its premium audio and lifestyle products. The collaboration combines Blaupunkt’s innovative product portfolio with Super Gifts’ experience in corporate gifting solutions. This partnership will enable companies to engage employees, reward achievements, strengthen client relations, and offer festive gifts with high-quality technology products.Under the agreement, Super Gifts will represent Blaupunkt’s corporate gifting business across major states including Maharashtra, Gujarat, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, West Bengal, Odisha, Assam, and other eastern and southern regions.Sukhesh Madaan, CEO of Blaupunkt Audio India, said: “Corporate gifting has gone beyond conventional merchandise to showcase a company’s dedication to providing value for money in terms of high-quality experience. The collaboration with Super Gifts is a major milestone in establishing a strong footprint within the corporate gifting space.”Rehan Azad, MD of Super Gifts, added: “It gives us immense pleasure to collaborate with Blaupunkt Audio India, a brand that stands for innovation and high-quality products.The trend in corporate gifting is moving towards technology-based gifts, and Blaupunkt’s product range is the best fit.”The partnership will drive corporate sales across Blaupunkt’s range of wireless earbuds, headphones, speakers, soundbars, and lifestyle technology products. These offerings will cater to enterprises, channel partners, employee rewards programs, customer engagement initiatives, and festive gifting campaigns.
Article Summary: Super Gifts will represent Blaupunkt’s corporate gifting business across major states including Maharashtra, Gujarat, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, West Bengal, Odisha, Assam, and other eastern and southern regions.
